q: [Numerical] A metal crystallises in an FCC structure. a = 408 pm, M = 108 g/mol, Z = 4. What will be its density approximately? (Na = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical
topic: Solid State — Density of Unit Cell

q: If the cation/anion radius ratio is 0.50, what will be the coordination number and geometry?
explanation: The ratio 0.414–0.732 is for octahedral voids, so CN = 6 and an NaCl-type structure is formed.
subject: Physical

q: Which statement about the zinc blende (ZnS) structure is correct?
options: S²⁻ are in FCC and Zn²⁺ are in alternate tetrahedral voids; coordination is 4:4
Zn²⁺ are in FCC and S²⁻ are in all octahedral voids; coordination is 6:6
In ZnS there is only 1 formula unit per unit cell
explanation: In ZnS, S²⁻ form a CCP/FCC arrangement, Zn²⁺ occupy half the tetrahedral voids, Z = 4 and CN is 4:4.
subject: Physical

q: What colour does NaCl become due to an F-centre?
explanation: An electron trapped in an anion vacancy forms an F-centre, which gives NaCl a yellow colour.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a zero order reaction, [A]₀ = 0.20 mol L⁻¹ and k = 0.01 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. What will be its half-life (t₁/₂)?
explanation: For zero order, t₁/₂ = [A]₀/(2k) = 0.20/(2 × 0.01) = 10 s.
subject: Physical

q: In a second order reaction, what effect will doubling the initial concentration [A]₀ have on the half-life (t₁/₂)?
explanation: For second order, t₁/₂ = 1/(k[A]₀), so doubling [A]₀ halves t₁/₂.
subject: Physical

q: Which of the following is an example of a pseudo-first order reaction?
options: A bimolecular reaction between two gases
A saturated zero order reaction on a surface
explanation: Water being in excess, its concentration remains almost constant, so the actual second order reaction appears to be first order.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a first order reaction, t₁/₂ = 10 s. What will be its mean life approximately?
explanation: k = 0.693/10 = 0.0693 s⁻¹; mean life = 1/k ≈ 14.4 s, which is 1.44 × t₁/₂.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] In a solution, the mole fraction of the solute is 0.02 and the vapour pressure of the pure solvent is 100 mmHg. What will be the vapour pressure of the solution?
explanation: Relative lowering = x₂ = 0.02, so the decrease in pressure = 2 mmHg and the pressure of the solution = 100 − 2 = 98 mmHg.
subject: Physical
topic: Colligative Properties — Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure

q: [Numerical] What will be the boiling point elevation (ΔTb) for a 0.50 molal non-volatile solute solution? (Kb = 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹, i = 1)
subject: Physical
topic: Colligative Properties — Elevation of Boiling Point

q: [Numerical] The degree of dissociation (α) of CaCl₂ is 0.90. What will be its van't Hoff factor (i)?
explanation: For n = 3 particles, i = 1 + (n − 1)α = 1 + 2 × 0.90 = 2.8.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] What is the freezing point depression (ΔTf) for a 0.10 molal aqueous solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte? (Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a reaction at 298 K, ΔU = −100 kJ/mol and Δng = −2. What will ΔH be approximately? (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] In the adiabatic reversible expansion of 1 mol of a diatomic ideal gas (γ = 1.4) at 300 K, the volume becomes 8 times. What will be the final temperature approximately?
subject: Physical

q: Which statement about the heat of neutralisation is correct?
options: It is more negative for a weak acid
It is the same for all acid-base pairs
The heat of neutralisation is always positive
For a strong acid + strong base it is approximately −57.1 kJ/mol; for a weak acid/base it is less negative because some heat is spent in ionisation
explanation: The actual reaction is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; in a weak acid/base, heat spent in ionisation makes the value less negative.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] At 298 K, the equilibrium constant K = 10 for a reaction. What will ΔG° be approximately?
subject: Physical
topic: Thermodynamics — Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

q: For which reaction will Kp = Kc?
explanation: In H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI, Δng = 2 − 2 = 0, so Kp = Kc(RT)^0 = Kc. In the other reactions Δng ≠ 0.
subject: Physical
topic: Chemical Equilibrium — Kp and Kc Relation

q: [Numerical] For the reaction A ⇌ B, Kc = 4. Initially [A] = 1.0 M and [B] = 0. What will [B] be at equilibrium?
explanation: From Kc = x/(1 − x) = 4, x = 0.80, so at equilibrium [B] = 0.80 M.
subject: Physical

q: For an exothermic reaction, what effect will increasing the temperature have on the equilibrium constant (K)?
options: K will first increase then decrease
explanation: According to Le Chatelier, increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the endothermic direction, so the K of an exothermic reaction decreases.
subject: Physical
topic: Chemical Equilibrium — Temperature Effect on K

q: [Numerical] The molar solubility (s) of a salt of type AB₂ is 1 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹. What will be its solubility product (Ksp)?
explanation: For AB₂, Ksp = 4s³ = 4 × (10⁻³)³ = 4 × 10⁻⁹.
subject: Physical

q: In a two-component system, 2 phases are in equilibrium and the pressure is constant. By the reduced phase rule, what will be the degree of freedom (F')?
explanation: F' = C − P + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1, so the system is univariant.
subject: Physical

q: In a one-component system, what is the maximum number of phases that can coexist in equilibrium?
explanation: Setting F = C − P + 2 = 0 gives P = 3; more phases would make F negative, which is not possible.
subject: Physical

q: On the sublimation curve (OB) in the phase diagram of water, which phases remain in equilibrium and what is the degree of freedom?
explanation: On OB there is ice ⇌ vapour equilibrium; with P = 2, F = 1 − 2 + 2 = 1 (univariant).
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] The specific conductance (κ) of a 0.10 M solution is 0.020 S cm⁻¹. What is its molar conductance (Λm)?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] On passing 1 Faraday (1 F) of charge, how much copper (Cu) will be deposited from a Cu²⁺ solution? (Atomic weight of Cu = 63.5)
explanation: The equivalent weight of Cu = 63.5/2 = 31.75 g, and 1 F liberates 1 gram-equivalent of a substance.
subject: Physical

q: Which statement about standard electrode potential (E°) is correct?
options: On multiplying the coefficients of the equation, E° does not change, because it is an intensive property
On doubling the equation, E° also doubles
E° does not depend on temperature
explanation: Potential is an intensive property; ΔG changes, E° does not. E° can also be negative and can change with temperature.
subject: Physical

q: Which of the following is the correct order of first ionisation enthalpy (increasing order)?
explanation: First ionisation enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹) are approximately Al 578 < Mg 738 < Si 787 < P 1012. Al is lower than Mg because its outer electron is in a 3p orbital rather than the stable filled 3s² subshell, and P is highest because of its stable half-filled 3p³ configuration.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the shape of ClF₃?
explanation: ClF₃ has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs; the lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, so the shape is T-shaped.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the bond order of the O₂⁻ ion?
explanation: The bond order of O₂ is 2; one extra electron goes into a π* antibonding orbital, so bond order = (10 − 7)/2 = 1.5.
subject: Inorganic

q: The aqueous solution of which ion is colourless?
explanation: The configuration of Zn²⁺ is d¹⁰; a d–d transition is not possible, so the solution is colourless.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the Effective Atomic Number (EAN) of [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻?
explanation: EAN = atomic number − oxidation state + 2 × number of ligands = 26 − 2 + 12 = 36, which is equal to Kr.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which species is amphiprotic, i.e. can behave as both an acid and a base?
explanation: HCO₃⁻ can give H⁺ to form CO₃²⁻ and take H⁺ to form H₂CO₃; CO₃²⁻ is only a base and NH₄⁺ is only an acid.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which metal ion is at the centre of chlorophyll?
explanation: At the centre of the porphyrin ring of chlorophyll is Mg²⁺; Fe²⁺ is in haemoglobin.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which is the most stable free radical?
explanation: In the benzyl radical, the unpaired electron is delocalised by resonance in the benzene ring, so it is more stable than even a tertiary radical.
subject: Organic

q: How many stereoisomers in total are there of CH₃–CHBr–CHBr–CH₃ (2,3-Dibromobutane)?
explanation: It has one meso form and one enantiomeric pair, a total of 3 stereoisomers.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the lowest-energy (most stable) conformation of n-butane?
explanation: In the anti staggered conformation, both methyl groups are farthest apart, so torsional and steric strain are minimum.
subject: Organic

q: Which alkene gives only acetone on ozonolysis?
explanation: Both sides of (CH₃)₂C=C(CH₃)₂ have (CH₃)₂C= groups, so ozonolysis gives only 2 molecules of acetone.
subject: Organic

q: Who is the most reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substitution?
explanation: The –CH₃ group activates the ring by the +I effect and hyperconjugation; –NO₂ and –Cl deactivate the ring.
subject: Organic

q: In the reaction of 2-bromobutane with alc. KOH, which is the major product?
explanation: By the Saytzeff rule, the more substituted alkene is formed; trans-But-2-ene, being more stable than cis, is the major product.
subject: Organic

q: Which of the following compounds does NOT give the iodoform test?
explanation: The iodoform test requires a CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– group; formaldehyde has no methyl group, so it does not give the test.
subject: Organic

q: Who forms a diazonium salt with NaNO₂ + HCl at 0–5 °C?
explanation: Only a primary aromatic amine (aniline) forms a stable diazonium salt; an aliphatic primary amine is destroyed giving N₂ gas.
subject: Organic

q: How many hydrogen bonds are there between Guanine (G) and Cytosine (C) in DNA?
explanation: The G–C pair has 3 hydrogen bonds, while the A–T pair has 2 hydrogen bonds.
subject: Organic

q: [Numerical] At 300 K, what will be the average translational kinetic energy of 1 mol of an ideal gas? (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
explanation: Average translational KE = (3/2)RT = 1.5 × 8.314 × 300 = 3741 J ≈ 3.74 kJ.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a reaction, rate = k[A]². On increasing [A] 3 times, how many times will the rate increase?
explanation: Rate is proportional to the square of [A], so the rate will increase 3² = 9 times.
subject: Physical

q: Which colligative property is most suitable for determining the molar mass of proteins and other macromolecules, and why?
options: Osmotic pressure, because it gives a large, accurately measurable value even at the very low concentrations at which macromolecules dissolve
Elevation of boiling point, because proteins are stable on heating
Depression of freezing point, because it gives the largest change
Relative lowering of vapour pressure, because it is independent of temperature
explanation: Osmotic pressure is used for macromolecules because, unlike the elevation of boiling point or the depression of freezing point, it is large enough to measure accurately at very low concentrations, and it is measured at room temperature, so the solute is not heated or damaged.
subject: Physical

q: How many effective atoms are there in an FCC (face-centred cubic) unit cell?
explanation: 8 corners × 1/8 + 6 faces × 1/2 = 1 + 3 = 4 atoms per unit cell.
subject: Physical

q: In which process is the increase in entropy the greatest?
explanation: On changing directly from a solid to a gas, disorder increases the most; in the other three processes entropy decreases.
subject: Physical

q: In the exothermic Haber process N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, which condition is best to increase the yield of NH₃?
explanation: In an exothermic reaction, low temperature favours the forward direction and high pressure favours the direction with fewer gaseous moles (to the right).
subject: Physical
topic: Chemical Equilibrium — Haber Process, Le Chatelier

q: Which of the following is an example of homogeneous catalysis?
options: Fe catalyst in the Haber process
explanation: In ester hydrolysis, H₂SO₄ is in the same phase (liquid) as the reactants; in the other three, the catalyst is solid and the reactants are gas/liquid.
subject: Physical

q: What is the phenomenon of scattering of light by colloidal particles called?
explanation: The path of a light ray passing through a colloidal solution is visible due to the Tyndall effect.
subject: Physical

q: According to Fajans rules, which compound will have the most covalent character?
explanation: Li+ is the smallest cation, its polarising power is the greatest, so LiCl has the most covalent character.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is formed on reducing KMnO4 in a strong alkaline medium?
explanation: In a strong alkaline medium, MnO4- takes one electron to form green MnO4 2-, in which the oxidation state of Mn is +6.
subject: Inorganic

q: When is rain called acid rain?
options: When its pH is equal to 7.0
When its pH is less than 6.8
When its pH is less than 5.6
When its pH is less than 7.0
explanation: Due to CO2, the pH of normal rain is about 5.6; when the pH falls below 5.6 due to SO2 and NOx, it is called acid rain.
subject: Inorganic

q: The Mond process is used for the refining of which metal?
explanation: In the Mond process, Ni + 4CO forms volatile Ni(CO)4, which on heating gives pure Ni.
subject: Inorganic

q: According to the Huckel rule, which species is aromatic?
explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion has 6 pi-electrons and is cyclic, planar and conjugated, so by the (4n+2) rule it is aromatic.
subject: Organic

q: In the chlorobenzene + NaNH2 / liq. NH3 reaction, what is formed via the benzyne intermediate?
explanation: Attack of NH2- on the benzyne intermediate forms aniline; this is the elimination-addition mechanism.
subject: Organic

q: At which position does electrophilic substitution occur preferentially in pyrrole?
explanation: Electrophilic substitution in pyrrole occurs preferentially at the 2-position (α-position), because the intermediate formed by attack at C-2 is stabilised by resonance to a greater extent than the intermediate formed by attack at C-3.
subject: Organic

q: Which aldehyde does NOT reduce Fehling solution?
explanation: The aromatic aldehyde benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling solution, but gives a silver mirror with Tollens reagent.
subject: Organic

q: Acetic acid dimerises completely in benzene. What is its van't Hoff factor (i)?
explanation: Two acetic acid molecules associate to form one dimer particle, so the number of particles is halved and i = 1/2 = 0.5. The observed molar mass is therefore twice the normal molar mass.
subject: Physical

q: What does a compressibility factor Z < 1 mean?
explanation: Z = PV/RT; Z < 1 means the gas shows less volume than ideal due to intermolecular attraction.
subject: Physical

q: What is the packing efficiency of an FCC (face-centred cubic) crystal?
explanation: The packing efficiency in FCC is 74%, in BCC 68% and in simple cubic 52.4%.
subject: Physical

q: Multilayer adsorption is possible in which type of adsorption?
explanation: Physisorption occurs by weak van der Waals forces and can form multilayers; in chemisorption, due to the chemical bond only a monolayer is formed.
subject: Physical

q: For 1 mol of an ideal gas, what is the value of CP - CV?
explanation: For an ideal gas, CP - CV = R, where R is the gas constant.
subject: Physical

q: According to Henry law, what is the effect on the solubility of a gas?
options: The solubility of a gas increases on increasing pressure
The solubility of a gas is always independent of temperature
The solubility of a gas decreases on increasing pressure
The solubility of a gas is independent of pressure
explanation: According to Henry law, the solubility of a gas is proportional to its partial pressure, so solubility increases on increasing pressure.
subject: Physical

q: For the hydrogen-like ion He+ (Z = 2), what is the ionisation energy of the electron in the ground state? (Energy of an electron in the nth orbit = -13.6 Z^2/n^2 eV)
explanation: For He+ in the ground state, E1 = -13.6 x 4 / 1 = -54.4 eV, so the energy needed to remove the electron to infinity is 54.4 eV.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which hydrogen halide has the greatest ionic character?
explanation: Ionic character follows the electronegativity difference between H and the halogen, which is largest for HF. The difference and the ionic character decrease down the group to HI.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is the B-F bond in BF3 shorter than the sum of the single-bond covalent radii of boron and fluorine?
options: p-pi-p-pi back bonding from a filled 2p orbital of fluorine into the vacant 2p orbital of boron gives the bond partial double-bond character
BF3 is a purely ionic compound
Boron uses sp3 hybridisation in BF3
Strong hydrogen bonding occurs between BF3 molecules
explanation: Back donation of a fluorine lone pair into the vacant p orbital on boron gives the B-F bond partial double-bond character and shortens it. BF3 remains a covalent, trigonal planar molecule with sp2 hybridised boron.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which carbonate decomposes on heating to give the metal oxide and carbon dioxide, whereas the carbonates of sodium, potassium, rubidium and caesium are stable to heat?
explanation: The small Li+ ion strongly polarises the large carbonate ion and distorts it, so Li2CO3 decomposes to Li2O and CO2 on heating. The larger alkali metal cations polarise the carbonate ion much less, so their carbonates are stable to heat.
subject: Inorganic

q: In the solid state, PCl5 exists as which pair of ions?
explanation: Solid PCl5 is ionic, [PCl4]+[PCl6]-, with a tetrahedral cation and an octahedral anion. This differs from gaseous PCl5, which has a trigonal bipyramidal covalent structure.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why are interstitial compounds of transition metals, such as steel and TiH2, much harder than the pure metals?
options: Small atoms such as H, B, C or N occupy interstitial voids in the metal lattice, distort it and hinder the slipping of metal layers
The small atoms replace metal atoms in the lattice by substitution
Interstitial compounds are ionic salts with no metallic bonding
The small atoms form separate molecular units with no effect on the lattice
explanation: Small atoms trapped in the voids distort the close-packed metal lattice and make dislocation movement difficult, which increases hardness. The metallic bonding, lustre and conductivity of the metal are largely retained.
subject: Inorganic

q: In [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] and [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6], the NH3 and CN- ligands have been interchanged between the complex cation and the complex anion. What is this type of isomerism called?
explanation: The ligands are redistributed between the cationic and anionic complex ions, with NH3 and CN- interchanged between the two metals. This interchange of ligands between two complex ions is coordination isomerism.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE) of a tetrahedral d7 complex, ignoring pairing energy? (In a tetrahedral field, the e set lies at -0.6 Delta-t and the t2 set at +0.4 Delta-t.)
explanation: A tetrahedral d7 ion has the configuration e4 t2^3, so CFSE = 4(-0.6 Delta-t) + 3(+0.4 Delta-t) = -1.2 Delta-t.
subject: Inorganic

q: In aqueous solution, HCl, HNO3 and HClO4 appear equally strong. What is this effect called, and why does it occur?
options: Common ion effect, because the acids share a common ion
Buffer action, because water resists pH change
Levelling effect, because water accepts a proton from every strong acid completely and levels them all to the strength of H3O+
Salt hydrolysis, because the acids form salts with water
explanation: Water is a sufficiently strong base to accept a proton from all strong acids completely, so in water they are all levelled to H3O+. Their real differences in acid strength appear only in a less basic, differentiating solvent such as glacial acetic acid.
subject: Inorganic

q: In carbonic anhydrase, which metal ion at the active site catalyses the hydration of carbon dioxide to bicarbonate?
explanation: Carbonic anhydrase contains Zn2+ bound to three histidine residues and a water molecule. The zinc-bound hydroxide attacks CO2, giving bicarbonate and regenerating the enzyme.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which compound exists appreciably in the enol form at equilibrium, because its enol is stabilised by conjugation and intramolecular hydrogen bonding?
explanation: The enol of acetylacetone is stabilised by a conjugated C=C-C=O system and by a six-membered intramolecular hydrogen-bonded ring. Simple ketones such as acetone exist almost entirely in the keto form.
subject: Organic

q: Propanone (CH3COCH3) and propanal (CH3CH2CHO) have the same molecular formula but different functional groups. Which term describes their relationship?
explanation: Both have the molecular formula C3H6O but different functional groups, a ketone and an aldehyde. Compounds with the same formula but different functional groups are functional isomers.
subject: Organic

q: Which reactive intermediate is formed when chloroform is treated with aqueous NaOH, and is involved in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction?
explanation: Chloroform is deprotonated to the trichloromethyl anion, which loses chloride to give dichlorocarbene, :CCl2. This electrophilic carbene attacks phenoxide in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
subject: Organic

q: What is the major product of the hydration of propyne with dilute H2SO4 in the presence of HgSO4?
explanation: Water adds to propyne by Markovnikov addition to give the enol prop-1-en-2-ol, which tautomerises to propanone. The product is therefore the methyl ketone, not an alcohol.
subject: Organic

q: Benzene, on treatment with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 and CuCl, gives which product?
explanation: This is the Gattermann-Koch reaction, a formylation of benzene in which a -CHO group is introduced directly onto the ring. The product is benzaldehyde.
subject: Organic

q: 2-Bromobutane, on treatment with the bulky base potassium tert-butoxide, gives mainly which alkene?
explanation: The bulky base abstracts the less hindered hydrogen on the primary carbon, so the less substituted alkene predominates. This is the Hofmann product, overriding the usual Saytzeff preference for the more substituted alkene.
subject: Organic

q: Propan-1-ol, on oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in dichloromethane, gives mainly which product?
explanation: PCC oxidises a primary alcohol to the aldehyde and stops at that stage. In the absence of water the aldehyde is not oxidised further to the carboxylic acid.
subject: Organic

q: Acetophenone, on treatment with hydrazine followed by KOH in ethylene glycol with heating, gives which product?
explanation: This is the Wolff-Kishner reduction, in which the carbonyl group is reduced to a methylene group. The -COCH3 group of acetophenone is therefore converted to -CH2CH3, giving ethylbenzene.
subject: Organic

q: Ethylamine, on treatment with NaNO2 and dilute HCl at 0 degrees C, gives mainly which products?
explanation: A primary aliphatic amine forms a diazonium salt that is unstable even at 0 degrees C and loses nitrogen at once. The carbocation left behind is captured by water, giving ethanol.
subject: Organic

q: In the vulcanisation of natural rubber, heating with sulphur produces which change in the polymer?
options: Conversion of the rubber into Bakelite
Cross-links of sulphur between polyisoprene chains
explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links between neighbouring polyisoprene chains, creating a three-dimensional network. This increases tensile strength and elasticity and improves resistance to heat and organic solvents.
subject: Organic

q: A gas has the van der Waals constant b = 0.0400 L mol-1. What is its critical volume Vc? (Vc = 3b)
subject: Physical

q: In the fluorite (CaF2) structure, what are the positions of the ions and their coordination numbers?
options: Ca2+ ions in all octahedral voids and F- ions in a face-centred cubic arrangement, coordination 6:6
Ca2+ ions in a face-centred cubic arrangement and F- ions in all tetrahedral voids, coordination 8:4
Ca2+ ions in a simple cubic arrangement and F- ions in a body-centred arrangement, coordination 8:8
F- ions in a face-centred cubic arrangement and Ca2+ ions in half the tetrahedral voids, coordination 4:8
explanation: In CaF2, Ca2+ ions form a face-centred cubic lattice and F- ions occupy all eight tetrahedral voids. Each Ca2+ is surrounded by eight F- ions and each F- by four Ca2+ ions, giving 8:4 coordination.
subject: Physical

q: In the titration of oxalic acid with KMnO4 in acidic medium, the reaction is slow at first and then speeds up. Which species acts as the autocatalyst?
explanation: Mn2+ is formed as the reaction proceeds and catalyses the reaction itself, so the rate increases once Mn2+ has built up. This self-catalysis is autocatalysis.
subject: Physical

q: Red blood cells placed in pure water swell and burst (haemolysis), whereas in 0.9% NaCl solution they retain their shape. Why?
options: Pure water is hypertonic, so water leaves the cells
0.9% NaCl is hypotonic, so water leaves the cells
Both liquids are isotonic, so the cells burst for another reason
Pure water is hypotonic, so water enters the cells by osmosis, whereas 0.9% NaCl is isotonic and there is no net flow of water
explanation: The cell fluid is more concentrated than pure water, so water enters the cells by osmosis until they burst. A 0.9% NaCl solution has the same osmotic pressure as the cell fluid, so no net osmosis occurs.
subject: Physical

q: For a reaction, Delta-H = -80 kJ mol-1 and Delta-S = -160 J K-1 mol-1. What is Delta-G at 300 K, and is the reaction spontaneous at this temperature?
explanation: Delta-G = Delta-H - T Delta-S = -80 - 300 x (-0.160) = -32 kJ mol-1. Since Delta-G is negative, the reaction is spontaneous at 300 K.
subject: Physical

q: For PCl5 dissociating as PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2, the theoretical molar mass of PCl5 is 208.5 g mol-1 and the observed average molar mass at equilibrium is 139.0 g mol-1. What is the degree of dissociation, alpha? (alpha = (Mt - Mo) / (Mo x (n - 1)), n = 2)
explanation: alpha = (208.5 - 139.0) / 139.0 = 69.5 / 139.0 = 0.50. The observed molar mass is lower than the theoretical value because one molecule gives two particles on dissociation.
subject: Physical

q: Why does solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) sublime at atmospheric pressure instead of melting?
options: Because the triple-point pressure of CO2, 5.11 atm, is above atmospheric pressure, so liquid CO2 cannot exist at 1 atm and the solid passes directly to vapour
Because CO2 molecules have no intermolecular forces at all
Because the triple-point temperature of CO2 is above room temperature
Because solid CO2 decomposes into carbon and oxygen on heating
explanation: At 1 atm, below the triple-point pressure of 5.11 atm, heating solid CO2 crosses the sublimation curve rather than the fusion curve. Liquid CO2 can exist only at pressures above 5.11 atm.
subject: Physical

q: In the standard hydrogen electrode, what are the conditions and the standard electrode potential?
options: Platinum electrode, H2 at 1 atm, H+ at 0.1 M, E-degree = 0.00 V
Platinum electrode, H2 at 1 atm, H+ at 1 M, E-degree = 0.00 V
Copper electrode, H2 at 1 atm, H+ at 1 M, E-degree = +0.34 V
Zinc electrode, H2 at 1 atm, H+ at 1 M, E-degree = -0.76 V
explanation: The standard hydrogen electrode uses a platinum electrode in contact with hydrogen gas at 1 atm and H+ ions at 1 M concentration. Its standard potential is fixed at 0.00 V by convention.
subject: Physical

q: What are the units of the rate constant k for a second-order reaction, rate = k[A]^2, with rate in mol L-1 s-1?
explanation: k = rate / [A]^2, so its units are (mol L-1 s-1) / (mol2 L-2) = L mol-1 s-1.
subject: Physical

q: For a sparingly soluble salt, if the ionic product Q exceeds the solubility product Ksp at a given temperature, what happens?
options: No precipitate forms, because the solution is unsaturated
More solid dissolves until Q equals Ksp
Ksp increases until it equals Q
Precipitation occurs until Q falls to Ksp
explanation: When Q exceeds Ksp the solution is supersaturated with respect to the salt. Solid therefore precipitates out until the ionic product falls to the Ksp value.
subject: Physical

q: Using Slater's rules, what is the effective nuclear charge (Zeff) felt by the 3s electron of sodium (Z = 11, configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1)?
explanation: Screening S = 2(1.00) for the 1s electrons + 8(0.85) for the n = 2 electrons = 8.80, so Zeff = 11 - 8.80 = 2.20; 8.80 is the screening constant itself, not Zeff.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which of the following oxides is the most acidic?
explanation: Acidity of oxides increases across a period as the central atom becomes more electronegative and its oxidation state rises; Cl(VII) in Cl2O7 gives the most acidic oxide, while Na2O is basic and Al2O3 is amphoteric.
subject: Inorganic

q: Hydrogen chloride has an observed dipole moment of 1.08 D and an H-Cl bond length of 127 pm. Taking the dipole moment of a fully ionic H+Cl- pair as 4.80 D per angstrom of bond length, what is the approximate percentage ionic character of the H-Cl bond?
explanation: Fully ionic moment = 4.80 x 1.27 = 6.10 D, so percentage ionic character = (1.08 / 6.10) x 100 = 17.7%, about 18%; the bond is therefore predominantly covalent.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is carbon dioxide linear whereas sulphur dioxide is bent (angular)?
options: Carbon has no lone pair and two bond pairs, giving a linear arrangement, whereas sulphur has two bond pairs and one lone pair, which bends the molecule
Both molecules have the same number of lone pairs on the central atom
Carbon dioxide has one lone pair on carbon and sulphur dioxide has none
Carbon dioxide is sp3 hybridised and sulphur dioxide is sp hybridised
explanation: In CO2 the central carbon has only two electron domains and no lone pair, so VSEPR gives 180 degrees; in SO2 the lone pair on sulphur occupies a third domain, compressing the O-S-O angle to about 119 degrees.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why does NCl5 not exist, whereas PCl5 exists?
options: Nitrogen is too large to fit five chlorine atoms around it
Phosphorus is more electronegative than nitrogen
Nitrogen, a second-period element, has no vacant d orbitals and cannot expand its octet beyond eight electrons, whereas phosphorus can use 3d orbitals
NCl5 would be ionic and chlorine cannot form ionic bonds with nitrogen
explanation: Nitrogen can form at most four covalent bonds within an octet because its valence shell has only s and p orbitals; phosphorus, in the third period, has vacant 3d orbitals available to expand its octet to ten electrons in PCl5.
subject: Inorganic

q: In chromium pentoxide, CrO5, four oxygen atoms are present as peroxide oxygens (oxidation state -1) and one as an oxide oxygen (oxidation state -2). What is the oxidation state of chromium?
explanation: Let the oxidation state of Cr be x: x + 4(-1) + (-2) = 0, so x = +6; counting all five oxygens as -2 would wrongly give +10.
subject: Inorganic

q: How many geometrical isomers does the octahedral complex [Co(NH3)3Cl3] have, and what are they called?
explanation: The three NH3 ligands can occupy one face of the octahedron (fac) or a meridian plane through the metal (mer); these are the only two distinct geometrical arrangements, and neither involves a change of donor atom.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the conjugate base of the dihydrogen phosphate ion, H2PO4-?
explanation: A conjugate base is formed by removing one proton from the acid, so H2PO4- loses H+ to give HPO4 2- with the charge lowered by one; H3PO4 is its conjugate acid and PO4 3- has lost two protons.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is eutrophication, and what is its main effect on a lake?
options: Acid rain dissolving limestone and raising the pH of the lake
Enrichment of water with nitrates and phosphates, causing algal blooms whose decay depletes dissolved oxygen and kills aquatic life
Depletion of stratospheric ozone by chlorofluorocarbons, increasing ultraviolet radiation
Accumulation of carbon dioxide, warming the lake water
explanation: Excess nutrients from fertilisers and sewage stimulate algal growth; when the algae die and decompose, bacteria consume dissolved oxygen, so fish and other aquatic organisms die from oxygen depletion.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which metal is the oxygen carrier in haemocyanin, the respiratory pigment of many molluscs and arthropods, and what colour is the oxygenated pigment?
explanation: Haemocyanin binds oxygen at a pair of copper(I) centres, oxidising them to copper(II) in a peroxide-bridged form that is blue, unlike the red iron-based haemoglobin.
subject: Inorganic

explanation: The cis isomer has a symmetry plane bisecting the C1-C2 bond and passing through the third ring carbon, so it is achiral. The trans isomer has no plane or centre of symmetry, and its mirror images are non-superimposable, so it occurs as an enantiomeric pair.
options: The cis isomer is optically active and the trans isomer is optically inactive
The trans isomer is a meso compound
The cis isomer is achiral, while the trans isomer exists as a pair of enantiomers
Both the cis and trans isomers are achiral
q: Which statement about 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane is correct?
subject: Organic

explanation: Bromine forms a cyclic bromonium ion on one face of the double bond, and bromide attacks from the opposite face. This anti addition to the cis alkene gives the (2R,3S) form, which has a centre of symmetry and is meso.
q: Bromine is added to cis-but-2-ene. What is the major dibromide formed?
subject: Organic

explanation: Protonation gives a resonance-stabilised allylic carbocation. Bromide attack at the internal carbocation centre is faster and gives the 1,2-addition product, the kinetic product at low temperature; the more substituted 1,4-addition product predominates on warming.
q: Hydrogen bromide is added to buta-1,3-diene at low temperature. What is the major product?
subject: Organic

explanation: Cyanide is an ambident nucleophile. In covalent AgCN the nitrogen end attacks, so the product is the isocyanide CH3CH2NC; ionic KCN would attack through carbon and give the nitrile.
q: Bromoethane is heated with silver cyanide (AgCN). What is the main organic product?
subject: Organic

explanation: Periodic acid cleaves the carbon-carbon bond of a vicinal (1,2-) diol. Each CH2OH carbon is oxidised to an aldehyde, so one molecule of the diol gives two molecules of formaldehyde.
q: Ethane-1,2-diol is treated with periodic acid (HIO4). What is the main organic product?
subject: Organic

explanation: This is the Clemmensen reduction. Under strongly acidic conditions the carbonyl group is reduced directly to a methylene group, so C=O becomes CH2 and cyclohexanone gives cyclohexane.
q: Cyclohexanone is heated with zinc amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid. What is the main product?
subject: Organic

explanation: A beta-keto acid decarboxylates readily on heating through a six-membered cyclic transition state. Loss of CO2 from CH3COCH2COOH leaves the enol of acetone, which tautomerises to acetone.
q: 3-Oxobutanoic acid is heated. What are the main products?
subject: Organic

explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction: cuprous chloride catalyses replacement of the diazo group by chlorine, with nitrogen gas expelled, so the diazonium salt is converted into chlorobenzene.
q: Benzenediazonium chloride is treated with cuprous chloride in concentrated hydrochloric acid. What is the main organic product?
subject: Organic

explanation: In an alpha-helix the carbonyl oxygen of residue i is hydrogen-bonded to the NH hydrogen of residue i+4. This regular backbone hydrogen bonding holds the helix together; disulphide bonds stabilise tertiary structure, not the helix itself.
options: Hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen of one residue and the NH hydrogen four residues further along the chain
Salt bridges between charged side chains only
Hydrophobic interactions between side chains only
q: What stabilises the alpha-helix secondary structure of a protein?
subject: Organic

explanation: Homolysis of benzoyl peroxide is initiation, not propagation. In propagation the chain-carrying radical adds to the C=C bond of a monomer, generating a new radical at the chain end, and this addition repeats to build the polymer chain.
options: Two growing chains combine, ending chain growth
Monomer molecules join with loss of a small molecule such as water
The growing carbon radical adds repeatedly to the double bond of further styrene molecules, lengthening the chain
Benzoyl peroxide splits into phenyl radicals
q: In the free-radical polymerisation of styrene started by benzoyl peroxide, what happens in the propagation step?
subject: Organic

q: [Numerical] One mole of a real gas (van der Waals constants a = 1.36 L² atm mol⁻² and b = 0.0318 L mol⁻¹) occupies 1.00 L at 300 K. What is its pressure? (R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical

explanation: For a cubic crystal d = a/√(h² + k² + l²). For the (200) planes, d = a/√4 = a/2, so a = 2 × 204 pm = 408 pm.
q: [Numerical] For a cubic crystal, the interplanar spacing for the (200) planes is 204 pm. What is the lattice parameter a?
subject: Physical

explanation: For a second-order reaction t1/2 = 1/(k[A]0) = 1/(0.050 × 0.40) = 1/0.020 = 50 s.
q: [Numerical] A second-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.050 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ and initial concentration [A]0 = 0.40 mol L⁻¹. What is its half-life?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] The rate constant of a reaction becomes 3 times larger when the temperature is raised from 300 K to 310 K. What is the activation energy Ea approximately? (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] A 0.20 molal aqueous solution of MgCl2 is 80% dissociated. What is the freezing point depression of the solution? (Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical

explanation: By the first law, ΔU = q + w. Work done by the system is negative, so ΔU = 500 + (−320) = +180 J.
q: [Numerical] A gaseous system absorbs 500 J of heat and does 320 J of expansion work on the surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For the equilibrium N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g), the equilibrium partial pressures are p(N2O4) = 0.40 atm and p(NO2) = 0.80 atm. What is Kp?
subject: Physical

explanation: At constant volume the partial pressures of N2, H2 and NH3 do not change, so the reaction quotient is unchanged and there is no shift. K changes only with temperature.
q: For the gaseous equilibrium N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), an inert gas is added at constant temperature and constant volume. What happens to the position of equilibrium?
subject: Physical

explanation: By the phase rule F = C − P + 2 = 1 − 1 + 2 = 2, so temperature and pressure can both be varied independently.
q: In a one-component system, how many degrees of freedom are there in a region where only a single phase is present, for example only liquid water?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] How long must a current of 0.965 A be passed to deposit 1.08 g of silver from a solution containing Ag+ ions? (Molar mass of Ag = 108 g mol⁻¹; F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical
